problem: Existing open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs either lack hierarchy (ConceptGraphs), lack object-object relationship reasoning (HOV-SG), or build relations offline from complete point clouds, so none supports online, hierarchical, relationship-aware task reasoning.
motivation: Tasks like 'ensure exits are not blocked' or 'prepare the room for a meeting' need reasoning about object interactions, not just object search. The paper attaches VLM-derived relation features to a Hydra-style hierarchy so an LLM/VLM pipeline can decide which subtasks are needed and feasible.
key_idea: Build an incremental five-layer Hydra scene graph with CLIP open-vocabulary features on objects and rooms and VLM visual-encoder relation features on object-object edges, then run an LLM+VLM+LLM pipeline over it for task reasoning.
insight: Storing VLM visual-encoder features (not text) on edges lets the language part of the VLM be queried lazily at task time, keeping online graph construction light (<1 s/frame on a Jetson Orin). The VLM choice matters: DeepSeek-VL2 reaches SR 84-100 on tasks 1-4 versus 40-55 for InstructBLIP. Colored bounding-box inpainting plus naming the colors in the prompt keeps the VLM on the intended object pair (qualitative Fig. 4); no numeric ablation of this is given. Object retrieval also improves over ConceptGraphs and HOV-SG, but the comparison uses filtered baselines and different object counts.
method: Hierarchical graph: Hydra builds a 5-layer graph (mesh, object, place, room, building) online, with Kimera semantics, Voxblox TSDF/ESDF and GVD places; rooms are detected by dilation and pruning.

Object features: YOLOe gives boxes, masks and labels; the CLIP ViT-L/14 embedding is a weighted sum of masked crop, box crop and label text. Features are attached to the mesh and then running-averaged into object nodes.
Room features: CLIP embeddings of full RGB frames are assigned to rooms by pose containment, then K-Means clustered into K feature clusters per room.

Object relations: for each object pair, DeepSeek-VL2's visual encoder processes the union-box crop with boxes inpainted in unique per-label colors. The features are stored on object-object edges and running-averaged.
Task reasoning LLM: o3 parses the task into relevant objects, subtasks and feasibility prompts as JSON, guided by a system prompt with examples.
Object/room search: CLIP cosine similarity against object features with a threshold, then a check that a relation edge exists. Rooms are selected by the average of K×N similarities.
VLM reasoning + decisor: VL2 evaluates each subtask using the relation features and a prompt naming the box colors. GPT-4o then decides whether the subtask should be executed.

setting.backbone: YOLOe + CLIP ViT-L/14 + DeepSeek-VL2 (frozen); o3 (task-reasoning LLM) and GPT-4o (subtask decisor), all frozen
setting.observation: RGB-D + odometry (RealSense D455, Ouster LiDAR, VN100 IMU)
setting.action_space: high-level task reasoning; navigation to detected objects via graph-based planner (GBPlanner)
setting.simulator: Replica and HM3DSem (offline object-retrieval evaluation); real world for the task-reasoning experiments
setting.privileged: none at test time (ground-truth objects were manually annotated for evaluation only)

numbers.extra: baselines filtered of background objects for fairness; own object detector gives far fewer objects (88.33)

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 runs per task; T1, T2 on quadruped, T3, T4 human-carried; T5 object search SR 100, FP 1.8±0.4

numbers.extra: pooled over 103 positive and 96 negative subtasks

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark is used. Runtime is in Table 4: the VL2 visual encoder takes 214-278 ms per frame, and graph construction takes 145-276 ms.
results: On HM3DSem, object retrieval reaches AUC 92.49 versus 87.27 for ConceptGraphs, and on Replica AUC 87.23 versus 80.50. In real-world tasks, SR is 84-100 with under 1 false positive per task (task 5, object search, has 1.8). DeepSeek-VL2 clearly beats InstructBLIP, and pooled subtask accuracy is 79.3%.
limitations: Task reasoning is evaluated only on a few self-designed real-world tasks with small samples, with no standard benchmark and no baseline for relational reasoning.
Accuracy on multi-object subtasks is modest (pooled 79.3%, task 4 at 74.9%). The pipeline is stochastic and depends on cloud LLMs and the VLM language head.

Relations are only computed for pairs visible in a single frame, and the pairwise VLM cost grows quadratically with the number of detected objects. The retrieval comparison is not object-count matched.
